title: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)

sections.label: Budget cut for digital transformation
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce Head Q of the Estimates by $100, noting Singapore's steady digital transformation progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head Q of the Estimates by reduced by $100." Singapore is progressing surely and steadily in our digital transformation.

sections.label: Digital inclusion and social cohesion
sections.summary: Singapore must ensure the less digitally savvy are not left behind, which could widen the digital gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Yet, to preserve social cohesion and inclusive growth, Singapore also must ensure that the less digitally savvy amongst us are not inadvertently left behind or excluded from participating and benefiting from digitalisation, which could widen the gap between those who know and know‐not.

sections.label: Digitalisation with empowerment and inclusion
sections.summary: It asks how the Government will ensure public and private sectors go digital with empowerment and inclusion as prerequisites.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: How will the Government ensure that the public and private sectors will go digital with empowerment and inclusion as prerequisites?

sections.label: Child Online Safety Index findings
sections.summary: The 2020 Child Online Safety Index found almost 60% of children aged eight to 12 in 30 countries faced at least one cyber risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: The inaugural 2020 Child Online Safety Index report found that almost 60% of children aged between eight and 12 in 30 countries were exposed to at least one form of cyber risk, of which 45% were affected by cyberbullying.

sections.label: Measures to reduce online harm
sections.summary: It asks what support measures and resources exist to raise awareness, prevent and intervene to reduce online harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: What are the support measures and resources available to raise awareness, prevent and intervene to reduce online harm?

sections.label: Protecting Singaporeans from online harm
sections.summary: It welcomes the Alliance for Action on online harms and asks what targeted measures MCI will put in place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The elderly, too, are not spared from being cyber victims.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I welcome the Alliance for Action to tackle online harms, especially those targeted at women and girls.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What are some targeted measures that MCI will put in place to protect the different segments of Singaporeans from varied forms of online harm?

sections.label: Online harms and OCBC phishing scam
sections.summary: All segments of the community are vulnerable to online harms, such as the recent OCBC phishing scam where 790 customers lost $13.7 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All segments of the community are vulnerable to online harms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We all know the recent OCBC phishing scam where 790 customers lost $13.7 billion.

sections.label: IMDA schemes for business digitalisation
sections.summary: IMDA schemes like BDDB, DLP and CTO-as-a-Service help brick-and-mortar businesses pivot to hybrid models, and MCI is asked how it will continue supporting digital capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The launch by IMDA of schemes, such as Better Data-Driven Business (BDDB), the Digital Leaders Programme (DLP) and the Chief Technology Officer (CTO)-as-a-Service, have created platforms to help many brick-and-mortar businesses pivot towards hybrid online-offline models and are, certainly, welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: How will MCI continue supporting businesses to build or enhance their digital capabilities, so as to take advantage of the post-COVID-19 phase of economic recovery?

sections.label: Taxpayers supporting SPH Media Trust
sections.summary: The speaker was surprised that taxpayers may pay up to $900 million over five years to support SPH Media Trust, the Government-owned publisher of most mainstream newspapers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I was surprised to learn at the February Sitting that taxpayers may have to pay up to $900 million over five years to support Singapore Press Holdings (SPH) Media Trust, the Government-owned publisher of most of Singapore's mainstream newspapers.

sections.label: Government arrangement with SPH Media Trust
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government's arrangement with SPH is a bad deal as taxpayers foot SPH Media Trust's bill while SPH's property assets are likely sold to Cuscaden Peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thus, it is reasonable to expect SPH to continue to fund the transformation of the media business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government's arrangement with SPH is evidently a bad deal as taxpayers have to foot the bill of SPH Media Trust at least for the next five years while the property assets of SPH, which are worth at least $3.9 billion and expected to generate an annual cash flow of $300 million, according to one broker's estimate, are likely to be sold to Cuscaden Peak, a company owned by our local property magnate Ong Beng Seng, for the benefit of existing and future shareholders.

sections.label: DPTM certification numbers and queue
sections.summary: Certification can take up to one year with a queue, and as of 2 March 2022, 81 organisations have attained DPTM certification out of about half a million registered entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, an organisation can take up to one year to get the certification, with a queue to start assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: As of 2 March 2022, there is a total of 81 organisations which have attained DPTM certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: ACRA records state that we have about half a million registered entities.

sections.label: Online mandatory theory test access
sections.summary: The online mandatory theory test for PMD and Power Assisted Bicycle riders was first launched only via laptop, though more people now have smartphones than laptops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: When the online mandatory theory test for PMD and Power Assisted Bicycle riders was first launched, it was only available via a laptop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Ironically, more people nowadays have a smart phone but not a laptop.

sections.label: Digital adoption and training figures
sections.summary: PayNow reached 3.07 million users in 2021, 4.4 million use Singpass, 118,000 were trained under TeSA, and 74% of firms adopted a digital solution in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: PayNow mobile users grew to 3.07 million people in 2021, 4.4 million people use Singpass, 118,000 people have been trained under TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) and 74% of firms have adopted at least one digital solution in 2020.

sections.label: Seniors and Hawkers Go Digital
sections.summary: The seniors and Hawkers Go Digital programme has run for two years, but some seniors and hawkers remain apprehensive about going digital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: In particular, the seniors and Hawkers Go Digital programme have been running for the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: However, there are still seniors and hawkers who are apprehensive about going digital.

sections.label: Children's first Internet device age
sections.summary: A 2019 survey found Singaporean children get their first Internet-enabled device at age eight, two years younger than the global average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to a survey in 2019, Singaporean children get their first Internet-enabled device at the tender age of eight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: That is two years younger than the global average and is amongst the youngest worldwide.

sections.label: Compulsive sexual behaviour help cases
sections.summary: WE CARE Community Services reported compulsive sexual behaviour help cases rose from 50 in 2019 to 100 in 2020, including excessive online pornography consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While most people use the Internet and social networking sites for gainful posted purposes, for work, learning and leisure, some, inadvertently fall prey to ills that lurk in our online spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: WE CARE Community Services, a community-based addiction recovery centre reported an increase in the number of people seeking help for compulsive sexual behaviour, including excessive online pornography consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: From 50 cases in 2019, WE CARE handled 100 cases in 2020.

sections.label: Loot box odds
sections.summary: The odds for some loot boxes are sometimes as low as 0.00005%, with four zeros behind the decimal point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The odds for some of these loot boxes are sometimes as low as 0.00005% – and that is four zeros behind the decimal point, for the record.

sections.label: AfA stakeholder consultation
sections.summary: The launch of AfA came after 300 stakeholders from diverse backgrounds were consulted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The launch of AfA came after 300 stakeholders from diverse backgrounds were consulted.

sections.label: Alliance for Action online harms
sections.summary: MCI says the AfA starts with 48 members across sectors in five work streams, and asks for updates on its progress and stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: According to MCI, the AfA will start with 48 members across the people, public and private sectors to address the issue of online harms in five key work streams as suggested by participants from the earlier conversations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Namely, they include public education, research, victim support, youth engagement and volunteerism clusters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I am encouraged by the launch of the AfA as it signifies our commitment to addressing online harms in an increasingly lethal society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I would thus like to ask the Minister for Communication and Information if she could share any updates on the progress of the AfA since its launch last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Additionally, could MCI also elaborate on the number of stakeholders it has managed to get on board the AfA since its launch?

sections.label: SME digitalisation initiatives and funding
sections.summary: Lists initiatives like IDPs, InvoiceNow, BDDB and SGTraDex to help SMEs digitalise, with $200 million added in Budget 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: To help our SMEs stay competitive, innovate and seize opportunities in the digital economy, there are a host of initiatives and resources to make going digital simple and easy for all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: These include schemes like: (a) the Industry Digital Plans (IDP), which are industry-specific, step-by-step guides to digitalisation; (b) InvoiceNow, which enables businesses to digitalise the way they transact; (c) Better Data Driven Business (BDDB) or Business Intelligence (BI) tools, help SMEs gain deeper insights by converting business data into visual dashboards for easier data analysis; and (d) the Singapore Trade Data Exchange (SGTraDex) – which is an open digital infrastructure that facilitates trusted sharing of data between supply chain ecosystem partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As part of Budget 2022, an additional $200 million will be allocated to enhance schemes that build digital capabilities in businesses and workers.

sections.label: SME digital programmes
sections.summary: The Government offers programmes such as the Productivity Solutions Grant and CTO as a Service to help SMEs go digital.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government has made available a wide range of programmes available to help SMEs to go digital, such as the Productivity Solutions Grant and CTO as a Service.

sections.label: Employee digital skills and reskilling
sections.summary: Employees need to go digital, be reskilled and upskilled, and use these skills at work, with room to raise take-up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To ensure sustained performance, the employees need to go digital, be reskilled and upskilled, and, importantly, must have the opportunity to use these digital skills in their daily work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While the expansion of SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit eligibility will help more companies provide these employees, there is a lot of room to increase the take-up amongst those already eligible.

sections.label: Tech and innovation manpower
sections.summary: Asks for an update on Singapore's tech and innovation manpower and whether enough Singaporeans will fill gaps in three to five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: As such, I would like to ask for an update on the tech and innovation manpower situation in Singapore now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Over the next three to five years, will we have enough Singaporeans to fill those gaps?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: What else will be done to address the gaps so that good tech firms remain invested in Singapore and continue investing in our people?

sections.label: Women in tech and STEM
sections.summary: Asks about female representation in tech jobs, tech leadership, STEM courses in IHLs in 2021 and IMDA talent programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Having enough women in tech can shape how girls think of a career in tech – that it is not just for the boys – and give them confidence to give it a shot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Hence, what is the female representation in tech jobs and tech leadership positions in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: What is the female representation in STEM‐related courses in IHLs in 2021 and across IMDA's talent programmes?

sections.label: Broader workforce digital skills need
sections.summary: The speaker said in the Budget debate that beyond specialised tech roles, the broader workforce needs knowledge and ability to use technologies as more non-ICT jobs are disrupted and digitalised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: In my Budget debate speech, I spoke about the fact that, beyond specialised tech roles, the broader workforce will need to be equipped with the knowledge and ability to use technologies in the workplace as an increasing number of jobs in non-ICT sectors are disrupted, digitalised and require the use of technologies.

sections.label: MCI support for digital capabilities
sections.summary: The passage asks how MCI will support the uplifting of the broader workforce's digital capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: How will MCI support the uplifting of the broader workforce's digital capabilities?

sections.label: Singapore technology infrastructure and adoption
sections.summary: Singapore ranks among the top countries for technology infrastructure and adoption, with Asia's highest average Internet connection speed and 4G subscriptions almost one and a half times its population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Chairman, Singapore ranks among the top countries for technology infrastructure and adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We have the highest average Internet connection speed in Asia and the number of 4G subscriptions in Singapore is almost one and a half times that of our population.

sections.label: Next-bound digital infrastructure developments
sections.summary: The passage states the current S-curve is saturated and asks what next-bound digital infrastructure developments Singapore can expect to build and sustain a vibrant Digital Economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: The current S‐curve is saturated and we need to get onto the next.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Hence, to build and sustain a vibrant Digital Economy, what are the next‐bound digital infrastructure developments that Singapore can expect?

sections.label: MCI international action on attacks
sections.summary: The passage states an attack in one area can have widespread ramifications and asks what MCI is doing internationally to address these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: An attack in one area can have widespread ramifications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Therefore, what is MCI doing in the international arena to address these challenges?

sections.label: ICT sector and professional growth
sections.summary: Since 2016 the Information and Communications Sector grew an average of 9.4%, above GDP growth, and ICT professionals rose from around 180,000 in 2016 to 216,000 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since 2016, the Information and Communications Sector has grown by an average of 9.4%, well above the GDP growth rate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Across the economy, the number of ICT professionals has risen from around 180,000 in 2016 to 216,000 in 2020.

sections.label: Digital comfort and cybersecurity gaps
sections.summary: MCI surveys show 76% of Singaporeans comfortable with digital tech, but only 40% installed cybersecurity apps and 40% of seniors recognise phishing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: According to surveys carried out by MCI, 76% of Singaporeans said they feel comfortable using digital technologies, but only 40% have installed cybersecurity apps on their mobile phones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Among seniors aged 60 and above, 67% use instant messaging and over half search for information online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: But only 40% could recognise and avoid phishing attempts.

sections.label: New online safety Codes of Practice
sections.summary: Codes of Practice in three new areas will require platforms to minimise children's and young persons' exposure to harmful content.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To raise the baseline standard for online safety, we plan to introduce Codes of Practice in three new areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It will require platforms to have robust systems in place to minimise exposure of children and young persons to harmful content.

sections.label: New Codes have force of law
sections.summary: The new Codes of Practice will have the force of law, similar to existing IMDA-administered Codes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Similar to existing Codes of Practice administered by IMDA, these new Codes will have the force of law.

sections.label: Ukraine situation heightens risks
sections.summary: Given the unfolding situation in Ukraine, Singapore must be alive to heightened risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Given the unfolding situation in Ukraine, we must be alive to the heightened risks.

sections.label: Rise in data breach incidents
sections.summary: Between 2020 and 2021, Singapore saw a 73% increase in reported data breach and ransomware incidents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Between 2020 and 2021, Singapore observed a 73% increase in reported data breach and ransomware incidents.

sections.label: Colonial Pipeline ransomware attack
sections.summary: The ransomware attack on US Colonial Pipeline last year caused fuel shortages across the US East Coast.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The ransomware attack on US Colonial Pipeline last year, for example, caused fuel shortages across the US East Coast.

sections.label: Virtual assets as CII
sections.summary: Virtual assets such as cloud-hosted systems must be recognised as critical information infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With the shift to virtualisation, we must be able to recognise virtual assets as CII, too, such as systems hosted on the cloud.

sections.label: Risk-based infrastructure protection review
sections.summary: A risk-based approach to protect infrastructure and services and enable quick recovery will be reviewed by 2023 with consultations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will consider how to apply a risk-based approach to protect these infrastructure and services and for them to recover quickly when attacked.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We intend to complete this review by 2023, factoring in stakeholder and public consultations.

sections.label: PDPA data breach penalties
sections.summary: PDPA amendments raised maximum financial penalties for data breaches, taking effect from 1 October 2022 with lead time for businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To uphold this trust, organisations must continue to take ownership and be held accountable, especially those that hold sizeable volumes of personal data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why the PDPA amendments in 2020 raised the maximum financial penalty for data breaches to $1 million, or 10% of local annual turnover, for organisations whose turnover exceeds $10 million, whichever is higher.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With sufficient lead time given to businesses, the penalties will now take effect from 1 October 2022.

sections.label: POFMA action on COVID-19 misinformation
sections.summary: POFMA was used 20 times to act swiftly on COVID-19-related misinformation and prevent falsehoods from taking root.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, POFMA allowed us to take swift action on 20 occasions to curb COVID-19-related misinformation and prevent falsehoods from taking root.

sections.label: Local media reach and monetisation
sections.summary: Mediacorp and SPH Media reach 96% of Singaporeans, but there are no easy answers on monetising this reach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Second, while our local media enjoys good reach – today, Mediacorp and SPH Media reach 96% of Singaporeans – there are no easy answers on how they monetise this reach.

sections.label: SPH Media Trust shareholder injection
sections.summary: Shareholders voted and agreed to an initial injection of $80 million cash and $30 million in shares for SPH Media Trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The shareholders voted and agreed to an initial injection of $80 million in cash and $30 million worth of shares for SPH Media Trust.

sections.label: Global content market growth
sections.summary: The global content market will grow to over $500 billion by 2025, half in Asia Pacific, and Singapore will support companies and talents through partnerships and technology.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The global market for content is set to grow to more than $500 billion by 2025, half of which is in the Asia Pacific.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Global names like Walt Disney, iQIYI, WarnerMedia and Netflix already have a presence here, alongside homegrown players like Beach House Pictures, one of Asia's largest independent production companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will continue to support these companies and our talents by: (a) exploring new partnerships with creator networks like Titan Digital Media, platforms like YouTube, TikTok and Twitch and online creators; (b) and partnering industry to improve content quality and better understand viewer preferences through data, artificial intelligence (AI) and virtual production.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These efforts will position us as a hub for content that is both "Made in Singapore" and "Made with Singapore".

sections.label: Secure vibrant digital future
sections.summary: MCI outlines priorities to govern and secure Singapore's digital space and engage Singaporeans, aiming to build a vibrant and secure digital future together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With the concerted efforts of the Government, industry and Singaporeans, I am confident that Singapore will be able to build a secure and vibrant digital future; and that the Little Red Dot that we all love will continue to shine brightly on the international stage!

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Chairman, I have outlined MCI's priorities to govern and secure our digital space and to engage Singaporeans in a digitalised world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These are critical building blocks for Singapore's continued survival and success.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We look forward to partnering all Singaporeans to build a vibrant and secure digital future together!

sections.label: Singapore household digital access
sections.summary: 98% of households have broadband access and 99% of households with children under 15 have computer access.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Singapore is a highly-connected society – 98% of households have access to broadband and 99% of households with children under 15 have access to computers.

sections.label: Assistance for low-income households
sections.summary: Since 2020, initiatives have assisted more than 34,000 low-income households with their digital access needs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Since 2020, these initiatives have assisted more than 34,000 low-income households with their digital access needs.

sections.label: Seniors and hawkers digital training
sections.summary: Since 2020, SDO's digital ambassadors trained over 130,000 seniors in basic digital skills and empowered 11,000 hawkers to adopt e-payment solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Since 2020, SDO's digital ambassadors have trained more than 130,000 seniors to adopt basic digital skills like using smartphones and empowered 11,000 hawkers to adopt e-payment solutions.

sections.label: Seniors smartphone ownership rate
sections.summary: Combined efforts of SDO and partners resulted in 84% of seniors reporting they own and use a smartphone daily.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The combined efforts of SDO and our partners have resulted in 84% of seniors reporting that they own and use a smartphone in their daily lives.

sections.label: Fund supports 22 projects
sections.summary: 22 projects have been supported under the fund, expected to benefit over 100,000 individuals across society.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Since then, 22 projects have been supported under the fund and are expected to benefit over 100,000 individuals across society.

sections.label: NLB loans and digital reach
sections.summary: At least 64% of residents visited a library or accessed NLB online content last year, and over 98,000 benefited from digital readiness programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Despite pandemic-related restrictions, NLB's steady loan numbers and growing digital reach exemplify the key role that they play, with at least 64% of Singapore's residents visiting a library or accessing NLB's online content last year and over 98,000 individuals benefiting from NLB's digital readiness programmes so far.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To this end, our libraries will be refreshed under the Libraries and Archives Blueprint 2025, or LAB25.

sections.label: NLB launches ExperienceIT
sections.summary: NLB will launch ExperienceIT with innovation and technology leaders such as Amazon Web Services to drive interest in emerging technology.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To realise the LAB25 vision, NLB will launch "ExperienceIT", in collaboration with leaders in innovation and technology, such as Amazon Web Services, to drive interest and confidence in more in-depth learning about emerging technology and partner the community to bring more Singapore stories to NLB's network of libraries and make more collections accessible to the public.

sections.label: Punggol Regional Library opening
sections.summary: The opening of Punggol Regional Library later this year marks another step towards enabling, empowering and equalising digital access.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The opening of Punggol Regional Library later this year marks another step towards enabling, empowering and equalising digital access.

sections.label: Mother tongue children collections grow
sections.summary: Over the past three years, NLB's mother tongue language collections for children have increased by 11%.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Over the past three years, NLB's mother tongue language collections for children have increased by 11%.

sections.label: New online safety Codes
sections.summary: Minister Josephine Teo shared that MCI will introduce new Codes of Practice to enhance online user safety.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In her speech, Minister Josephine Teo shared that MCI will be introducing new Codes of Practice to enhance online user safety.

sections.label: Digital Readiness Survey metrics
sections.summary: MCI is refining Digital Readiness Survey metrics to understand how well Singaporeans perform essential digital tasks.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To gain more in-depth understanding of our citizens' digital readiness, MCI is refining metrics and indicators to be tracked in the Digital Readiness Survey.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In addition to existing measurements of digital adoption and usage, we intend to better understand the extent to which Singaporeans are able to perform essential digital tasks.

sections.label: Sunlight AfA online harms
sections.summary: MCI launched Sunlight AfA, which studies online harms in Singapore and their impact on women and girls.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MCI also launched Sunlight AfA, which I co-chair with Senior Minister of State Sim Ann.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Since its launch, the AfA has been studying the incidence of online harms in Singapore and how they impact individuals, especially women and girls.

sections.label: 2021 Digital Readiness Survey findings
sections.summary: MCI's 2021 survey found 76% of Singaporeans comfortable with digital technologies and 80% saying technologies eased their lives.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: According to MCI's 2021 Digital Readiness Survey, 76% of Singaporeans feel comfortable using digital technologies, while 80% of Singaporeans acknowledge that digital technologies have made their lives easier.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: This is encouraging, but we can and will do more.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We stand ready to work with individuals, companies and partners in the people sector to realise the vision of a digitally-ready and inclusive society.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital programme
sections.summary: More than 80,000 firms have benefited from SMEs Go Digital since 2017, a quarter joining in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: More than 80,000 firms have benefited from the SMEs Go Digital programme since 2017, including a quarter of them coming on board in 2021 alone.

sections.label: InvoiceNow and PayNow adoption
sections.summary: Over 50,000 businesses adopted InvoiceNow since 2019, and over 90% of businesses adopted PayNow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: To Ms Jessica Tan's question, more than 50,000 businesses have adopted InvoiceNow since it was launched in 2019, and more than 90% of our businesses have adopted PayNow.

sections.label: Industry Digital Plans launched
sections.summary: Since 2017, 20 IDPs have been launched to guide digitalisation across sectors including accountancy, logistics and security.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Since 2017, we have launched 20 IDPs to guide digitalisation across sectors as diverse as accountancy, logistics and security.

sections.label: Grow Digital programme results
sections.summary: Grow Digital has helped over 2,500 firms access markets in 10 countries and build digital capabilities since 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Since launching in 2020, Grow Digital has helped more than 2,500 firms access markets in 10 countries, while building capabilities in digital marketing, business matching and door-to-door fulfilment.

sections.label: Digital sector economic contribution
sections.summary: The sector contributed $28.4 billion, 5.6% of GDP, and grew 12.2%, outpacing other sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Last year, the sector contributed $28.4 billion to the economy, accounting for 5.6% of our GDP and grew by 12.2%, far outpacing other sectors.

sections.label: ICT professionals and unfilled tech roles
sections.summary: About 216,000 ICT professionals are employed, half in ICT and half in non-ICT sectors, with 19,000 tech roles unfilled.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Our Digital Economy employs around 216,000 ICT professionals, with half of them in the ICT sector and the other half supporting digital transformation in non-ICT sectors like finance, manufacturing and retail.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Yet, 19,000 tech roles remain unfilled across the economy, particularly in roles like software engineering and development, but also across the entire tech value chain, from deep technical skills like AI and cybersecurity, to innovation-oriented roles in product development, and applied business roles like cloud migration and data analytics.

sections.label: Local IDT degree places increase
sections.summary: Local IDT degree places rose four-fold from 800 in 2010 to 3,300 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The number of local IDT degree places has risen four-fold from 800 in 2010, to 3,300 in 2021.

sections.label: Support for ITE and Polytechnic students
sections.summary: A structured end-to-end approach will start with 1,000 places over three years and a TeSA TIP Alliance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: To help others like Syurhan pursue their passion and realise their ambitions, we will put in place a structured end-to-end approach to better support our Polytechnic and ITE students, starting with 1,000 places over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will establish a TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) for ITE and Polytechnics (TIP) Alliance, comprising leading global tech companies, leading companies here and major hirers to galvanise industry support for this effort.

sections.label: Closing on digital economy moves
sections.summary: Moves to help businesses thrive digitally and nurture a future-ready digital workforce aim to lift all boats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in closing, our moves to help businesses thrive in a digital economy and nurture a future-ready digital workforce will help us ensure that the digital wave is one that lifts all boats.

sections.label: Global data generated by 2025
sections.summary: By 2025, the estimated amount of data generated globally is about 463 exabytes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: By 2025, the estimated amount of data generated globally is about 463 exabytes.

sections.label: 5G coverage in Singapore
sections.summary: Telcos achieved 50% nationwide outdoor coverage at the start of 2022, ahead of their end-2022 target, and nationwide 5G coverage by 2025 is on track.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Our telcos have stated that they have achieved 50% nationwide outdoor coverage at the start of 2022, ahead of their end-2022 target.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: And we are on track for nationwide 5G coverage in Singapore by 2025.

sections.label: 5G-enabled AR Smart Glasses trial
sections.summary: The trial developed 5G-enabled augmented reality AI-powered Smart Glasses that assist factory operators in assembly and inspection and improve training efficiency for new hires by 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The trial developed a 5G-enabled augmented reality (AR) solution in the form of AI-powered "Smart Glasses".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: These "Smart Glasses" assist factory operators in assembly and inspection, and also improve training efficiency for new hires by 50%.

sections.label: Broadband infrastructure investment
sections.summary: As mentioned by Minister Lawrence Wong in the Budget speech, infrastructure will be developed to deliver broadband speeds around 10 times faster than today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As mentioned by Minister Lawrence Wong in the Budget speech, we will invest in developing infrastructure to deliver broadband speeds around 10 times faster, compared to today, unlocking new possibilities for digital experiences and tools.

sections.label: Greener data centres Call for Application
sections.summary: IMDA and EDB will pilot a Call for Application to facilitate calibrated growth of data centres with best-in-class energy efficiency and decarbonisation practices, launched by the second quarter of 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: IMDA and the Economic Development Board (EDB) will pilot a Call for Application to facilitate the calibrated growth of data centres that possess the best-in-class techniques, technologies and practices for energy efficiency and decarbonisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Greener data centres will allow us to do so while, at the same time, supporting the growing needs of our digital economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This Call for Application will be launched by the second quarter of 2022.

sections.label: RIE 2025 Smart Nation plans
sections.summary: As part of the $25 billion RIE 2025 Plan, Smart Nation and Digital Economy domain plans build on past investments to drive research in digital technologies with transformative potential.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As part of the $25 billion Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2025 Plan, our plans for the Smart Nation and Digital Economy (SNDE) domain build on past investments to drive research in digital technologies with transformative potential.

sections.label: Future Communications Research Programme funding
sections.summary: IMDA and the National Research Foundation are investing $70 million in Singapore's first national Future Communications Research and Development Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: IMDA and the National Research Foundation are investing $70 million in our first national Future Communications Research and Development Programme (FCP).

sections.label: MOU with 6G Flagship
sections.summary: Under FCP, an MOU was signed with 6G Flagship, the world's first and leading 6G research programme funded by the Academy of Finland.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As part of FCP, we signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with 6G Flagship in July last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This is the world's first and leading 6G research and development programme funded by the Academy of Finland.

sections.label: Flexxon X-PHY AI SSD
sections.summary: Under this call, local cybersecurity company Flexxon developed X-PHY in 2021, the world's first SSD with AI cybersecurity defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Under this call, a local cybersecurity company, Flexxon, developed X-PHY in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It is the world's first solid state drive (SSD) enabled with an AI cybersecurity defence.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme for IoT
sections.summary: CSA launched the Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme for consumer IoT devices in October 2020, the first of its kind in Asia Pacific then.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: CSA launched the Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme (CLS) for consumer IoT devices in October 2020, the first of its kind in the Asia Pacific at that time.

sections.label: ASEAN Model Contractual Clauses
sections.summary: Singapore led development of the ASEAN Model Contractual Clauses for Cross Border Data Flows to let enterprises transfer personal data across borders with regulatory certainty.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Singapore has also made strong efforts to develop the interconnected data and AI ecosystems, striking a balance between data protection, data security and data innovation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We took the lead to develop the ASEAN Model Contractual Clauses for Cross Border Data Flows (MCCs) to enable enterprises to transfer personal data for business transactions across borders with regulatory certainty.

sections.label: AI governance partnerships and ASEAN guide
sections.summary: Building on Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework, Singapore partners with the US and UK and works with ASEAN on an AI governance and ethics guide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Building on Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework, we are partnering countries, such as the US and the UK to learn from international best practices and align AI governance principles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are also working with ASEAN member states to coordinate the development of an ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics.

sections.label: Online harms to children
sections.summary: Parents report cyberbullying, sexual harassment, sexual grooming and inappropriate content, with three main categories: sex, violence and self-harm or other dangerous acts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Or what could lead to them to be harmed, physically and emotionally?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And parents have told us it is cyberbullying, sexual harassment, sexual grooming and exposure to inappropriate content – and there are three main categories: sex, violence and self-harm or other dangerous acts.

sections.label: Women in tech statistics
sections.summary: Close to three in 10 students in IDT courses at IHLs are female, four in 10 tech professionals are women, and SG Women in Tech was started by IMDA in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Just to share some statistics and some updates, close to three in 10 of our students in our IDT courses, which I mentioned earlier, in our IHLs are female.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And according to a Boston Consulting Group (BCG) study, four in 10 of our tech professionals are women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The SG Women in Tech movement, which was mentioned by Ms Tin Pei Ling, was started and driven by IMDA in 2019.

sections.label: Programme reach and girls
sections.summary: Since its launch in October 2019, the programme has reached over 120,000 people and connected over 115,000 girls in schools with female tech leaders through Students Ask videos.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Just to share some statistics with Ms Tin, since its launch in October 2019, the programme has reached out to more than 120,000 people through its initiatives and connecting over 115,000 girls in schools with female tech leaders through a series of Students Ask videos.

sections.label: National AI Strategy launch
sections.summary: In 2019 the Government launched the National AI Strategy, and the National Artificial Intelligence Office under the Prime Minister's Office launched five national AI programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government recognises the rich potential of emerging technologies, like AI, to generate economic gains as well as to improve the lives of our people.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is why, in 2019, we launched the National AI Strategy and articulated the vision for Singapore to be a leader in developing and deploying scalable, impactful AI solutions in key sectors that are of high value and relevance to our businesses and our people.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Under the Prime Minister's Office, the National Artificial Intelligence Office (NAIO) launched an initial tranche of five national AI programmes.

sections.label: Singapore research citation ranking
sections.summary: Based on Field-weighted Citation Impact, an indicator used to assess research capabilities, Singapore ranks first in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If we base it on Field-weighted Citation Impact (FWCI) – it is an indicator that is commonly used to assess research capabilities – Singapore is actually first in the world, ranks number one.

sections.label: SPH Media Trust funding questions
sections.summary: The speaker asks about progress in getting private donors to fund SPH Media Trust and whether current and future SPH shareholders can enjoy windfall profits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: SPH has accumulated a huge amount of property assets from the profits generated from the near-monopoly print business in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, the decision that the Government has made, means that the Government is okay to allow the shareholders to take away all the assets and leave behind a $900 million baby for the taxpayer to be burdened with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The second clarification is when Minister S Iswaran presented this deal or this structure in Parliament some time ago, he also said that SPH Media Trust is going to have private donors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, may I ask the Minister what is the progress in getting these private donors to also fund SPH Media Trust?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Are the current shareholders and the future shareholders of SPH, the listed company, in a position to enjoy huge windfall profits going to some of those donors, that will help us out in the funding of SPH Media Trust?

sections.label: Public funding for SPH Media Trust
sections.summary: Public funding is needed for SPH Media Trust because it is not Government-owned but a company limited by guarantee.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It would be part of how other arms of the Government are funded and you would basically plan for it within the Ministry's block budget and be done with it.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But the fact that we are here explaining to Members the need to provide public funding to SPH Media Trust is precisely because it is not Government-owned.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is a company limited by guarantee (CLG).

sections.label: Media business leaving listed entity
sections.summary: The economics of the media business changed so much that remaining part of a listed entity is no longer tenable.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, Mr Leong suggests, or he seems to think, that it was an option for the media business to continue as part of the listed entity.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have explained on several occasions by now – in May 2021, in February this year and, indeed, just an hour or so ago – why the economics of the media business have changed so much that it is no longer tenable for them to remain in the previous structure, part of a listed entity, with other businesses because the investments that are going to be needed for the media part of the business to transform are going to be quite involved.

sections.label: Funding trusted local media
sections.summary: It asks whether up to $180 million a year to support trusted local media is excessive given the size of the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Because, is up to $180 million a year to support trusted local media an excessive amount given the size of our economy – for our people and our businesses to be able to see the world through our own unique lens, for our voice to be projected without impediment, for our cultures and our traditions to be expressed in the way we want it to be expressed?

sections.label: SMEs reskilling staff digital skills
sections.summary: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked about helping SMEs reskill their staff and workforce in digital skills when they transform digitally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Chairman, Ms Mariam Jaafar asked about helping our SMEs reskill their staff and workforce in terms of digital skills when they transform digitally.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital industry digital plan
sections.summary: The SMEs Go Digital industry digital plan is designed to account for these skills needs in the digital plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: First, as part of our SMEs Go Digital, our industry digital plan, which I spoke about earlier, they are designed to account for these skills needs in the digital plan.

sections.label: Expanding CET with IHLs
sections.summary: CET efforts with other Institutes of Higher Learning will expand to train smaller firms, as SMEs may face resource constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Looking ahead, we will continue to expand the Continuing Education Training (CET) efforts with other Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to provide training for smaller firms across the economy as smaller firms like SMEs may face resource constraints in sending their employees for this sort of skills training.

sections.label: SPH privatisation profit cost question
sections.summary: An MP asks how far the Government required SPH to transfer business segments so the CLG could be self-funded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I think the substance of what Mr Leong is getting at is about the privatisation of profits and the socialisation of costs to the taxpayer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, my question or clarification is: when SPH's proposal was considered by the Government, how far did the Government go to require SPH to transfer segments of its business which would allow the CLG to be self-funded as far as possible in view of the range of assets owned by the SPH group?

sections.label: Shareholders approve SPH Media Trust injection
sections.summary: Shareholders voted and agreed to an initial injection of $80 million cash and $30 million in shares for SPH Media Trust.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The shareholders voted and agreed to an initial injection of $80 million cash and $30 million worth of shares for SPH Media Trust.

sections.label: SPH Media Trust restructuring proposal passed
sections.summary: SPH Media Trust restructures a media business from a listed company, and the management's proposal passed muster with shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Ultimately, SPH Media Trust is a restructuring of a media business that existed within a listed company.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And so, as things go, it is the proposal that is made by the management to the shareholders that must pass muster.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And this was the proposal that passed muster.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is a matter of speculation whether the restructuring proposal could have gone through with an even higher contribution.
